classes.name: Basal Cell Carcinoma
classes.description: A common type of skin cancer that begins in the basal cells, typically appearing as a pearly or waxy bump on sun-exposed skin.

classes.name: Melanoma
classes.description: The most serious type of skin cancer, developing in the cells (melanocytes) that produce melanin. Often characterized by irregular moles.

classes.name: Benign Nevus
classes.description: A common benign skin growth, commonly referred to as a mole, composed of pigmented melanocytic cells.

classes.name: Seborrheic Keratosis
classes.description: A non-cancerous skin growth that typically appears as a waxy, scaly, or 'stuck-on' lesion on the face, chest, or back.

classes.name: Dermatofibroma
classes.description: A common, harmless, firm red-to-brown bump on the skin, typically found on the legs, representing a benign fibrous skin lesion.

classes.name: Vascular Lesion
classes.description: Benign growths of blood vessels in the skin, such as cherry angiomas, hemangiomas, or pyogenic granulomas.

classes.name: Actinic Keratosis
classes.description: A rough, scaly patch on the skin caused by years of sun exposure. It is a precancerous lesion that can turn into SCC if untreated.

classes.name: Squamous Cell Carcinoma
classes.description: A common form of skin cancer that develops in the squamous cells of the outer layer of the skin, often presenting as a firm red nodule.

classes.name: Unknown / Non-Diagnostic
classes.description: Insufficient structural patterns identified in the dermoscopic image to classify. Further imaging or clinical biopsy suggested.
